title: Telecom-Band Optical Transitions of Erbium Atoms in Rare-Gas Solids
authors: Evgenii Zaitsev, Alec Dinerstein, Shan Zou, Charles Peretti, Yutian Wen, Wei Guo, Gregory V. Hartland, Yizhong Huang, Dafei Jin
abstract: Rare-earth (RE) atoms, such as erbium (Er), have inner-shell optical transitions in the near-infrared, some of which are in the telecom bands. These transitions are largely insensitive to the host environment due to effective shielding by the filled outer shells. Cryogenic rare-gas (RG) solids, such as solid neon (Ne) and argon (Ar), combine high chemical purity with a nearly nuclear-spin-free environment, making them attractive solid hosts for preserving optical and spin coherence. In this work, we isolate neutral Er atoms in solid Ne and Ar at 6 K and characterize their emission by steady-state and time-resolved photoluminescence (PL) spectroscopy. In both hosts, we observe several near-infrared transitions between 1000--1500 nm, including inner-shell emission in the telecom O and E bands. The $4f \rightarrow 5d$ transition near 1299 nm forms a multiplet of narrow components, consistent with crystal-field splitting, and decays on a microsecond timescale. The $4f \rightarrow 4f$ transition near 1437 nm shows a matrix shift below 1 cm$^{-1}$ in both hosts. In solid Ne, its inhomogeneous linewidth is bounded by the spectrometer resolution to < 22 GHz, and its PL lifetime reaches up to 78.9 ms, close to the estimated radiative limit. Thermal annealing extends the 1437 nm lifetime in Ne and suppresses the phonon sidebands relative to the zero-phonon lines in Ar. These results identify RG solids as promising hosts for long-lived telecom-band Er emission and provide a foundation for future spin-photon interfaces and hybrid quantum architectures.
summary: The authors characterized the optical emission of Erbium atoms in solid Neon and Argon matrices using time-resolved PL spectroscopy. They found that the $4f ightarrow 4f$ transition in solid Ne exhibits extremely long lifetimes and narrow linewidths, indicating minimal environmental decoherence. This establishes rare-gas solids, particularly Ne, as excellent solid-state hosts for robust, telecom-band quantum emitters.
main_problem: The study aims to characterize the near-infrared, telecom-band optical transitions of Erbium (Er) atoms embedded in rare-gas (RG) solids to determine if these solids are suitable hosts for long-lived quantum emitters.
main_result: The research demonstrates that Er atoms in solid Ne exhibit exceptionally long photoluminescence lifetimes (up to 79 ms) and narrow spectral features for the $4f ightarrow 4f$ transition, establishing RG solids, particularly Ne, as promising platforms for quantum applications.
method: The work employed steady-state and time-resolved photoluminescence (PL) spectroscopy on samples of Er co-deposited with solid Ne and solid Ar, measured at cryogenic temperatures.
model_or_system: The physical system involves neutral Er atoms isolated within crystalline matrices of solid Neon (Ne) or solid Argon (Ar). The analysis compares the spectral signatures of the $4f ightarrow 5d$ (L13) and $4f ightarrow 4f$ (L14) transitions in both hosts.
key_observables: Near-infrared emission transitions (1000–1500 nm), PL lifetime (up to 79 ms), inhomogeneous linewidth (< 22 GHz), and spectral shifts relative to free-atom values.
important_parameters: Cryogenic temperature ($\approx 6$ K); the difference in host perturbation between Ne and Ar; the radiative limit for the PL lifetime.
main_assumptions: The observed spectral differences are attributed to the differential coupling strength between the $5d$ electron (strong coupling) and the shielded $4f$ electrons (weak coupling) to the host lattice.
figures_summary: Figure 1(a) shows the experimental setup, and Figure 1(b) provides an energy-level diagram for neutral Er. Figure 2 presents representative PL spectra of Er in solid Ar and Ne.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by characterizing the optical transitions in both Ar and Ne, contrasting the highly coupled $5d$ transition (L13) with the weakly coupled, long-lived $4f$ transition (L14). The comparison highlights the superior environment provided by solid Ne.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant to AMO physics and quantum optics as it experimentally validates a solid-state platform (RG solids) for achieving long coherence times in atomic emitters, crucial for quantum memory and quantum networking.
